This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:

Order
1.

A complaint under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. was lodged by second respondent - complainant
against eight accused persons.
2.  The petitioner was arrayed as the eighth accused.

The allegation as against eighth accused in the complaint is as follows:
"The Complainant above-named most respectfully states as follows :-
1] That, the Complainant is residing at the above address with her family.

The Accused No.1 is the mother and the Accused. No.2 to No.7 are the brothers and sisters of the Complainant.
2] That, the immovable property consisting of 121/2 Cents of land and building situated in NC: 2024:KHC:21024 Survey No. 101-12 (Part) of Old Idya Village and now Survey No. 60-2 (Part) of Katipalla Village of Mangalore Taluk, (as per R.T.C.4/236) with the building bearing Door No.4-214-A (4th Block, Katipalla Rehabilitation Colony Site No. 236) was originally belonging to the deceased father of the Complainant and Accused No.2 to No.7, i.e., husband of Accused No.1.

After the death of said Shaikabba, the said property has become the joint property of the Complainant and Accused No.1 to No.7, the said property have been in possession enjoyed of the Complainant and the Accused No. 1 to No. 7.
3] That in the year 2008 the Complainant filed a suit as per O.S.No.57/08 in the File of 1st Addl. Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Mangalore for partition of the said property.

sentences.text: Thereafter the people connected to the Accused No.8 and some others visited the said property.
On enquiry the Complainant came to know that the Accused are making attempts to sell the said property.
The said enquiry further revealed that the Accused have forged certain documents in respect of the said property.

In that connection, the Complainant got issued a Lawyer's notice dated 13.02.2009 to the Accused and the Complainant got published a Public Notice in a Kannada Daily newspaper, namely,
'Vartha Bharathi', dated NC: 2024:KHC:21024 12.02.2009.

In the reply dated 26.02.2009, issued by the Accused No.8, the said Accused claimed the mortgage of the said property to Accused No. 8 for Rs. 1,50,000/- [Rupees One Lakh & Fifty thousand only) through the deposit of an alleged "Release Deed" dated 27.08.2001 (document No. 2266/2001-02) which in turn was allegedly executed on the strength of an alleged "Deed of General Power-of-Attorney" dated 20.08.2001 allegedly executed in favour of Accused No.2 by the Complainant, Complainant's brother one Abdul Razak and the Accused No.4 and No.6.
The Complainant obtained a certified copy of the said "Release Deed" on 13.03.2009.

The Complainant was terribly shocked to know that the said "Deed of General Power-of-Attorney"
dated 20.08.2001 and the said "Release Deed"
dated 27.08.2001 are all forged documents."
3.

As could be seen from the averments in the complaint, the allegation essentially is that the eighth accused, as the Manager of the Bank, had secured a mortgage by deposit of title deeds and had given a loan of Rs.1,50,000/-.
This according to the complainant made the eighth accused liable, since it was her case that the NC: 2024:KHC:21024 release deed and the power of attorney which were executed were forged documents.
4. A reading of the above would clearly indicate that there is absolutely no allegation of forgery as against the Bank Manager, i.e., the present petitioner.

Merely because the petitioner as the Bank Manager had granted a loan by securing a mortgage on the basis of certain documents, he cannot be arrayed as an accused on the premise that the documents submitted to him were forged documents.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner - eighth accused also submits that accused Nos.3 to 7 had also filed Crl.P. No.8808/2017 before this Court and the proceedings as against them were also quashed.

6. Be that as it may, in my view, since there is absolutely no allegation indicating any act on the part of the petitioner in the alleged forgery, there is absolutely no justification to continue the proceedings as against the petitioner.

Consequently, the proceedings as against the NC:
2024:KHC:21024 petitioner - eighth accused shall stand quashed.

This petition is, accordingly,
allowed.
